# Kekkai — governed tailnet coordination — pricing

| resource | price | what you get |
|---|---|---|
| `/x402/acl/decide` | USD 0.001 | deny-by-default ACL evaluation with the organisation boundary applied first: same-tailnet grant, cross-tailnet peering, or a named refusal (:deny-by-default / :cross-tailnet / :peering-grant-missing) |
| `/netmap/verify` | free | Ed25519 signed-netmap envelope verification |
| `/health` | free | — |
| `/blueprint.edn` | free | — |

Paid in USDC on base over x402, verified by [https://x402.nexus](https://x402.nexus).

## Why verification is free

**`/netmap/verify`** — charging to check whether an artifact is authentic prices the one action that protects the buyer. A node that cannot afford to verify runs unverified, which is the failure this whole boundary exists to prevent.

## What one decision buys

The unit is one edge decision with the organisation boundary applied first. The
transcripts below are not illustrations: each one was produced by calling
`kekkai.itonami.decide/decide` while this file was generated, on the planes
`kekkai.itonami.decide-test` asserts against. A refusal is a paid answer too —
the three refusals are kept distinct because they call for different actions, and
collapsing them into one `denied` sends an operator to change a policy that
cannot possibly fix the problem.

### A grant exists — the edge is allowed

The answer carries the grant that allowed it, so an operator can see which line of policy is doing the work.

Request:

```edn
{:dst
 {:id "n-server", :tags ["tag:server"], :tailnet "default", :user "alice"},
 :plane
 {:peerings [],
  :policies
  {"acme"
   {:grants [{:dst ["tag:cache"], :ports ["*"], :src ["bob"]}],
    :tag-owners {"tag:cache" ["bob"]}},
   "default"
   {:grants
    [{:capabilities [:overlay :ssh],
      :dst ["tag:server"],
      :ports [22],
      :src ["tag:laptop"]}],
    :tag-owners {"tag:laptop" ["alice"], "tag:server" ["alice"]}}}},
 :src
 {:id "n-laptop", :tags ["tag:laptop"], :tailnet "default", :user "alice"}}
```

Answer:

```edn
{:allowed? true,
 :capabilities [:overlay :ssh],
 :dst "n-server",
 :dst-tailnet "default",
 :ports [22],
 :src "n-laptop",
 :src-tailnet "default",
 :src-unowned-tags [],
 :tailnet "default",
 :via :policy}
```

### No grant — :deny-by-default

Same tailnet, nothing granting this direction. The fix is a policy edit.

Request:

```edn
{:dst
 {:id "n-laptop", :tags ["tag:laptop"], :tailnet "default", :user "alice"},
 :plane
 {:peerings [],
  :policies
  {"acme"
   {:grants [{:dst ["tag:cache"], :ports ["*"], :src ["bob"]}],
    :tag-owners {"tag:cache" ["bob"]}},
   "default"
   {:grants
    [{:capabilities [:overlay :ssh],
      :dst ["tag:server"],
      :ports [22],
      :src ["tag:laptop"]}],
    :tag-owners {"tag:laptop" ["alice"], "tag:server" ["alice"]}}}},
 :src
 {:id "n-server", :tags ["tag:server"], :tailnet "default", :user "alice"}}
```

Answer:

```edn
{:allowed? false,
 :dst "n-laptop",
 :dst-tailnet "default",
 :reason :deny-by-default,
 :src "n-server",
 :src-tailnet "default",
 :src-unowned-tags [],
 :tailnet "default"}
```

### Two organisations, no peering — :cross-tailnet

Not a policy edit: the fix is a negotiation between two organisations, so it is refused under its own name.

Request:

```edn
{:dst {:id "a-cache", :tags ["tag:cache"], :tailnet "acme", :user "bob"},
 :plane
 {:peerings [],
  :policies
  {"acme"
   {:grants [{:dst ["tag:cache"], :ports ["*"], :src ["bob"]}],
    :tag-owners {"tag:cache" ["bob"]}},
   "default"
   {:grants
    [{:capabilities [:overlay :ssh],
      :dst ["tag:server"],
      :ports [22],
      :src ["tag:laptop"]}],
    :tag-owners {"tag:laptop" ["alice"], "tag:server" ["alice"]}}}},
 :src
 {:id "n-laptop", :tags ["tag:laptop"], :tailnet "default", :user "alice"}}
```

Answer:

```edn
{:allowed? false,
 :dst "a-cache",
 :dst-tailnet "acme",
 :from "default",
 :reason :cross-tailnet,
 :src "n-laptop",
 :src-tailnet "default",
 :src-unowned-tags [],
 :to "acme"}
```

### Peered and mutually approved — the edge is allowed

`:via :peering` rather than `:via :policy`; the peering that carried it is named.

Request:

```edn
{:dst {:id "a-cache", :tags ["tag:cache"], :tailnet "acme", :user "bob"},
 :plane
 {:peerings
  [{:a "default",
    :approved-by ["default" "acme"],
    :b "acme",
    :grants
    [{:dst ["tag:cache"],
      :from "default",
      :ports [443],
      :src ["tag:laptop"]}],
    :id "p",
    :status "active"}],
  :policies
  {"acme"
   {:grants [{:dst ["tag:cache"], :ports ["*"], :src ["bob"]}],
    :tag-owners {"tag:cache" ["bob"]}},
   "default"
   {:grants
    [{:capabilities [:overlay :ssh],
      :dst ["tag:server"],
      :ports [22],
      :src ["tag:laptop"]}],
    :tag-owners {"tag:laptop" ["alice"], "tag:server" ["alice"]}}}},
 :src
 {:id "n-laptop", :tags ["tag:laptop"], :tailnet "default", :user "alice"}}
```

Answer:

```edn
{:allowed? true,
 :capabilities [:overlay],
 :dst "a-cache",
 :dst-tailnet "acme",
 :from "default",
 :peering "p",
 :ports [443],
 :src "n-laptop",
 :src-tailnet "default",
 :src-unowned-tags [],
 :to "acme",
 :via :peering}
```

## When payment cannot be confirmed

The gate fails closed, including when the facilitator is unreachable: a verifier
that cannot reach `/verify` knows nothing about a payment, and "unknown" is not
"paid". The two closed doors are reported apart — `:facilitator-unreachable`
means wait, `:payment-invalid` means pay again — because one undifferentiated 402
would send a caller who already paid to pay a second time for the same resource.
